title: Relevancy of note on similar-origin-window-agent on window event loop
body:
https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#definitions-3:similar-origin-window-agent-3

> This specification does not currently describe how to handle the complications arising from navigating between similar-origin window agents. E.g., when a browsing context navigates from https://example.com/ to https://shop.example/.

Is this still relevant now that "unit of related similar-origin browsing contexts" has been removed? 

In the context of [similar-origin-window-agent](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#similar-origin-window-agent) it appears there is no complication, since the below is acknowledged by the spec:

> Two Window objects that are same origin can be in different similar-origin window agents, for instance if they are each in their own browsing context group.

At least as I understood it, previously the spec said to basically share event-loop at the level of a  "unit of related similar-origin browsing contexts" , and the "complication" was that this effectively meant that "browsing contexts" could go from one to the other, and then had to start sharing event-loops. 

Actually, I'm not sure I remember correctly, but there was something complicated related to navigation to an origin, and then having to move a BC from one "unit" to another. 

It now seems pretty clear that sharing of event-loop is done at the level of "Similar-origin window agent", and that they are themselves scoped by their initial [browsing-context-group](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#browsing-context-group). So that two BCs in two different groups will simply never have to share a "Similar-origin window agent" regardless of whether they share an origin at some point due to navigation. 

So it seems to me the spec now acknowledges that BCs cannot travel from one group to the other because of navigation, hence sharing event-loop will be scoped to the "original" group to which one belonged.
